title: Indian-Origin UC Santa Cruz Student Dies After Car Plunges Off California Cliff
excerpt: Alli R. Singh, 19, a psychology major, was killed when the vehicle she was riding in went off West Cliff Drive near the iconic Steamer Lane surf break and landed in the ocean.
body:
• Alli R. Singh, 19, an Indian-origin UC Santa Cruz psychology major, died on August 13 after the car she was riding in plunged off West Cliff Drive into the Pacific Ocean.
  • Rescue swimmers extracted Singh from the submerged vehicle, but she was pronounced dead after being transported to a hospital.
  • The male driver escaped with minor injuries; the Santa Cruz Police Department is investigating the circumstances of the crash.
  • Singh, the daughter of Ravneet Mahal and Gian Singh, was preparing to begin her third year at UCSC.

A 19-year-old Indian-origin student at the University of California, Santa Cruz was killed on August 13 when the car she was riding in careened off a cliff along Santa Cruz's iconic West Cliff Drive and plunged into the Pacific Ocean.

The Santa Cruz County Sheriff-Coroner identified the victim as Alli R. Singh, a psychology major who had enrolled at UCSC in June 2024 and was preparing to start her third year.

The Crash

Emergency services received a report at approximately 12:50 a.m. that a vehicle had gone off a cliff on West Cliff Drive near Steamer Lane, one of California's most famous surf breaks. The Santa Cruz Fire Department deployed all five of its units to the scene, along with three units from Central Fire District, a battalion chief from Scotts Valley Fire, and Santa Cruz police.

https://x.com/dna/status/2091875451153400080

When crews arrived, they found one individual — the male driver — who had escaped the vehicle with minor injuries. A second person remained trapped inside the submerged car. Four rescue swimmers worked to extract Singh from the vehicle in the churning ocean waters. She was transported to a nearby medical facility, where she was pronounced dead.

Dramatic images from the scene showed a red car being hoisted from the Pacific by a rescue crane as waves crashed against the rocky cliffs below.

Family Mourns

Singh's aunt, Monica Singh-Strohmeier, paid tribute to her niece in a Facebook post on August 15.

"Alli was a thriving 19 year old in the midst of starting her 3rd year at UC Santa Cruz. She was a very smart, beautiful and loving young lady and will be missed by all who crossed her path."

— Monica Singh-Strohmeier, Singh's aunt

Singh-Strohmeier asked the public to respect the family's wish for privacy. Singh is the daughter of Ravneet Mahal and Gian Singh.

University Response

UC Santa Cruz spokesman Scott Hernandez-Jason confirmed that university police were called to the scene when it was learned the victim was a student.

"We were heartbroken to learn that the victim was a UC Santa Cruz student," Hernandez-Jason said in a statement. "Our deepest condolences go out to the student's family and friends during this difficult time. We are providing support resources to those affected by this tragedy."

Investigation Continues

The Santa Cruz Police Department is leading the investigation into the circumstances and cause of the crash. West Cliff Drive is a winding coastal road with dramatic cliffs overlooking the Pacific Ocean. The stretch near Steamer Lane is particularly rugged, with sheer drops to the rocky shoreline below.

Authorities have not released details about what caused the vehicle to leave the roadway. The investigation remains active.
nri_angle: An Indian-origin university student in California was killed in a tragic car crash, highlighting the personal losses that reverberate across the diaspora community.
